title: Time Series Atlas
status: Eight investigations with reviewed exploratory follow-ups
question: Which time series methods answer useful questions once source conventions, information timing, and evaluation assumptions are made explicit?
one_liner: Question-led time series studies with visible critiques, verified corrections and reproducible evidence.
aim: Demonstrate analytical judgment through reproducible investigations and short process stories, with independent agent reviews before design, execution, and publication.
scope: Seven real-data investigations—CO₂, electricity, retail, oil, river flow, air quality and ECG—plus synthetic change-detection and sampling controls. Each includes a frozen design, retained results, figures, review evidence and a plain-language process story.
conclusion: New questions changed the answer: anchoring the CO₂ starting level improved forecasts, a retail median beat the original methods yet understated sales volume, and ECG scores varied across patient fold assignments.

summary.question: What changes when we challenge the question, measurements, and evaluation before trusting a time series result?
summary.result: The collection shows how data provenance, information timing, metric choice and independence assumptions change the answer.

headline.label: Three-year December CO₂ MAE, anchored recent fit
ECG forest macro F1, original assignment

finding: In the fixed electricity panel, the shared model worsened forecasts for {{test.pooled_worse_customers:d}} customers, increasing macro normalized error by {{electricity_effect:.2f}}% relative to separate regression. In the exploratory CO₂ follow-up, anchoring the observed starting level reduced three-year December MAE from {{co2_fixed:.3f}} to {{co2_fixed_anchored:.3f}} ppm for the all-history fit and from {{co2_recent:.3f}} to {{co2_recent_anchored:.3f}} ppm for the recent fit. These are revised-data hindcasts, not causal attribution.

The original retail comparison favored zero on normalized error and TSB on raw-unit error. A later, explicitly exploratory weekly-median comparator beat both on their respective error measures, yet substantially underpredicted total recorded sales. Leaving out the dominant sales code changed the raw-unit winner. Lower forecast error alone does not establish an inventory policy.

Adaptive oil variance forecasts beat the fixed baseline on QLIKE while direction forecasts lost to prevalence on Brier. A secondary variance loss reversed the ranking. Same-hour air-quality peers outperformed local persistence under simulated outages, with scoring limited by observed truth.

River high-day recall did not translate into equally high new-onset recall. Past weather added little at the longer date offset and brought more false-alert episodes; daily information assumptions limit warning claims.

The original ECG forest scored {{ecg_forest:.3f}} macro F1 versus the majority baseline’s {{ecg_majority:.3f}}, yet missed every fusion-group beat. It led macro F1 in every additional patient assignment, while the patient-bootstrap difference from logistic regression crossed zero. These checks reuse the same people; they do not provide a population guarantee or clinical validation.

Synthetic controls expose two different failures: persistent noise breaks frozen alert calibration, while regular thinning leaves equally strong frequency aliases. A clear peak is not proof of unique identification.

The process story preserves initial design risks, later source discrepancies, actual code and copy defects, missed review findings, and verified corrections. Agent agreement is not independent human validation.

traps.how: Forecasting and nowcasting use declared information cutoffs and training-only transformations. ECG is classification given expert beat centers, including the declared post-center waveform window; people remain separate across training and evaluation.
Power and interval labels are explicit. Provider DST conventions differ from sampled values, so calendar masks and a nominal-clock assumption are recorded.

Original designs were committed before fitting. Later exploratory comparisons were declared after seeing original outcomes and frozen before new runs. Every declared comparison is retained; no cohort or winning split is selected after results.

figures.caption: The exploratory weekly-median comparator improves both error measures while substantially underpredicting total recorded sales. Forecast accuracy and inventory decisions remain different questions.
The forest leads pooled macro F1 under every tested patient assignment, but its scores vary. Rare-class support differs across training and test folds; no best split is selected.
High-day and eligible-onset recall use different cohorts and weighting. Daily observations are assumed available the next morning; false alerts, missed rises and unscored days limit warning claims.

Every declared noise, frequency and sampling setting remains visible. Recovery of the planted frequency does not remove regular-thinning alias ambiguity; common search bands still use different frequency grids.

not_claimed: Universal model rankings, causal attribution, latent retail demand, realized savings or clinical benefit.
Operational reporting latency, an automatic ECG detector, or generalization to unobserved catchments.
Guaranteed future recovery of unchanged oil inputs; they require explicit free acquisition and are not mirrored.
Independent human validation or completion of conditional advanced-method extensions.
